$comment: The institution registry: every deployment this system is allowed to drive.
This exists because the CLI used to import its institution list from
target-app/data.ts - the mock application's own module, whose TenantConfig
carries accent colours, DOM id prefixes and the label vocabulary used to
*render* the fixture. None of that means anything for a real target, and
an institution that is not the fixture could not be expressed at all.
That was genuine coupling to the original target, and it is the one place
the adaptation found any. The fix is a registry the system owns: four
fields, no code, no rebuild. Onboarding institution number 2,001 is an
entry in this file plus an origin in policy.yaml.
baseUrl: an absolute URL, or a path beginning with / which is resolved
against the local fixture app (TARGET_APP_PORT). product/productVersion
identify the VENDOR BUILD, not the institution - that is what makes one
recording reusable across every institution running the same software.

$probesComment: How to provoke each declared outcome ON THIS DEPLOYMENT.
Probes belong to the institution, not to the verification script: which
member number does not exist, which share is on hold, what an invalid
amount looks like - all of that is a property of the target. The script
used to hardcode the fixture app's answers, which meant it could only
These are all NATURAL error paths. The host is shared with other
candidates and its System Settings screen sets fault injection globally,
so nothing here touches it; per-request ?inject= cannot reach a step the
flow arrives at by clicking, so the states below are provoked with
inputs instead - which is the more honest test anyway.
Two notes on values that look odd. The amount is 1.000, not a word: the
input is typed `money`, so a non-numeric string is refused at pre-flight
and the browser never opens - a probe that cannot reach the application
verifies nothing. And the deliberately wrong password lives here rather
than in the environment precisely because it is invalid; a probe cannot
provoke a credential rejection using the credential that works.

probes.name: amount the host will not accept
